page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-144 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on x86_64 architecture. The server provides 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 72 physical cores using an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at a base clock of 2.3 GHz. The processor features 504 MB of Level 3 cache, 2 MB of Level 2 cache per core, and hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. Memory capacity totals 288 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs or local NVMe storage drives are bundled with this instance type, requiring external persistent disks for storage needs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. In multi-core synthetic stress testing, the instance scores within the top ten percent of evaluated hardware, marked by 156,262.69 on stress-ng and 134,972.44 on PassMark CPU suite. Clang software compilation and ray tracing tests achieve top-tier marks with scores of 65,247.0 and 120,375.0 respectively. Memory bandwidth reaches 543.81 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 11,546.73 GB/sec on cached small-block operations. In caching and database workloads, Redis SET operations register over 207 million operations per second.

With its compute-skewed resource profile, the instance offers strong efficiency for CPU-bound tasks requiring rapid matrix operations and high parallelization. However, the lack of onboard NVMe storage and the lower memory allocation per core represent tradeoffs for memory-intensive relational databases or low-latency local disk caching. The c4-highcpu-144 instance is well-matched for large-scale distributed compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference using AMX acceleration, high-throughput static web serving, video encoding, and intensive scientific batch processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-144 is a compute-skewed virtual instance engineered for high-concurrency CPU workloads. Driven by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, it delivers 144 dedicated vCPUs across 72 physical cores alongside a substantial 504 MB L3 cache. The machine contains 288 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and includes hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It omits integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. In benchmarks, it exhibits top-tier multi-threaded processing, software compilation throughput, and memory bandwidth, reaching over 207 million Redis SET operations per second and 543.81 GB/sec uncached read speeds. While limited in memory depth per core, the configuration delivers maximum computational density, making it suitable for distributed code builds, CPU-based deep learning inference, batch analytics, and high-concurrency web serving.
